idiom_name: plain transform function / tagged template literal
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the Transformer collapses into an ordinary function (or tagged template literal) mapping domain objects to markup strings: template literals give interpolation and multi-line markup, and one small escape helper replaces the writer's encoding step. The browser's XSLTProcessor - importStylesheet, transformToFragment/transformToDocument - is the declarative alternative, but it exists only in browsers, not in Node. A transformer object is still justified when several output formats share a writer abstraction.
pitfalls: Template literals do not escape: every interpolated user value must pass through the escape helper or the page ships an XSS hole.
XSLTProcessor is browser-only and transformToFragment needs an owner document; server-side Node has no built-in XSLT, so that path cannot be shared.
Inserting the returned string with innerHTML re-parses it and can execute injected markup; prefer DOM APIs or a sanitizer at the insertion point.

variants.name: XSLTProcessor in the browser
variants.implementation_notes: The declarative alternative in browsers: parse the stylesheet with DOMParser, importStylesheet, then transformToFragment(xmlDoc, document) and insert the fragment; per-request values go through setParameter. Choose it when presentation is a stylesheet and the data can be serialized to XML in the page, and accept that the same code cannot run in Node.
pitfalls: The transform runs synchronously on the main thread: large stylesheets block rendering.
fetch() of the stylesheet and XML must complete before importStylesheet, otherwise the transform silently produces an empty result.
